name: Flatwoods
description: Flatwoods occur on flat to gently rolling terrain with seasonally saturated, poorly drained soils. Historically frequent low intensity fire helped maintain these communities.

name: Grasslands
habitats: Acidic Meadows Over Sandstone or Shale
description: Grasslands are open habitats occurring over shallow acidic or alkaline soils. Their open character was historically maintained by soil conditions, periodic fire, and grazing animals.

name: High Elevation Hardwood Forest
description: High elevation hardwood forests occur in Georgia's mountains, including cool, moist slopes above approximately 3,500 feet. These forests support valuable hardwoods, watershed protection, and sensitive species.

name: Slope and Mesic Forest
description: Slope and mesic forests occupy cool, shaded ravines, terraces, and north or east facing slopes. Their moist but generally unsaturated soils support diverse hardwood communities.

name: Rock Outcrops
description: Rock outcrops include exposed granite, sandstone, flint, kaolin, and limestone formations. These fragile sites often contain sparse vegetation, rare plants, and specialized ecological communities.

name: Isolated Forested Wetland
description: Isolated forested wetlands are seasonally or semi permanently flooded depressions that are often disconnected from surface streams. Their hydrology depends heavily on rainfall and surrounding runoff.

name: Mixed Pine Oak Woodlands
description: Mixed pine oak woodlands contain fire tolerant oaks and pines. Their canopy may range from relatively closed forest to open woodland, depending on fire history, soils, slope, and disturbance.

name: Oak Woodlands
description: Oak woodlands are generally dry, open communities on rocky or sandy soils north of the Fall Line. Historically, periodic fire maintained their open canopy and diverse grasses and flowering plants.

name: Pine Savanna
description: Pine savannas feature an open pine canopy with abundant grasses, flowering plants, and other ground vegetation. Frequent fire limits woody understory growth and maintains their biological diversity.

name: Wetlands Within Pine Savannas
description: These wetlands occur within pine savanna landscapes on poorly drained soils. Open canopies and saturated, nutrient poor conditions support grasses, sedges, orchids, pitcher plants, and other specialized vegetation.

name: Scrub and Sandhills
description: Scrub and sandhill habitats occur on deep, well drained sands, including ancient dune systems. They commonly support longleaf pine, scrub oaks, wiregrass, lichens, and rare plants and animals.

name: Seepage Wetland
habitats: Low Elevation Seepy Thickets and Wet Woods
description: Seepage wetlands occur near the bases of slopes or within swales where groundwater moves toward streams or draws. They may remain saturated for part of the year and support rare moisture dependent communities.
